name: American Water Works Company, Inc.
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated water/wastewater franchises across 14 states, inelastic essential demand, and irreplaceable long-lived infrastructure give a strong durable moat, but regulators cap allowed returns, affordability and rate-case lag limit pricing power, and the model requires continuous debt and equity funding for rate-base capex.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Strong regulated moat 8/10, but Tier F on owner's earnings — conservative OE is negative in 0/5 last years because rate-base capex exceeds OCF, so the OE DCF supports no hurdle at $131.71; F is a sector-model verdict, not a business-quality verdict.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated franchises — no competing water provider in served territories
Essential, inelastic demand for water and wastewater service
Irreplaceable infrastructure — mains and plants last generations, replacement cost is prohibitive
Rate-base model: authorized returns on invested capital drive 7-9% long-term EPS guidance
moat_against: Regulators cap allowed returns and impose rate-case lag — pricing power is granted, not owned
Affordability and political pressure as bills rise with PFAS, lead-line and main-replacement capex
Capex permanently exceeds operating cash flow — funded by rising debt and share issuance (share count +2.33%/yr)
Rising interest expense on debt-funded capital program
Essential Utilities merger needs remaining state approvals, expected close by end of Q1 2027
